title: The angel of the Lord in the Assyrian camp

tellings.quote: The angel of the Lord moves through the Assyrian [music] camp the night the siege breaks.
Then the angel of the LORD went forth, and smote in the camp of the Assyrians a hundred and fourscore and five thousand: and when they arose early in the morning, behold, they were all dead corpses.

plain: One night, while the Assyrian army was besieging Jerusalem, a being called the angel of the Lord passed through its camp, and by morning a vast number of soldiers were dead. Michels tells it himself on the show, in the line "The angel of the Lord moves through the Assyrian camp the night the siege breaks." He draws on the Bible, here the King James Version of 1611. If the story were read as Michels frames it, it would be an ancient account of a powerful visitor stepping into a war. The text, Isaiah 37:36, tells it this way: "Then the angel of the LORD went forth, and smote in the camp of the Assyrians a hundred and fourscore and five thousand: and when they arose early in the morning, behold, they were all dead corpses." The order of events is the same in both: the angel goes out at night, strikes the camp, and the siege ends with the soldiers dead.
